title: First Year Seminar: Classical Studies
subject: CLAS
description: Seminar on a theme relevant to Classical Studies. Approaches and sources for consideration are drawn from literature, history, or archaeology of the ancient Mediterranean, depending on the instructor and topic.
restrictions: Open only to newly admitted U0 or U1 students.

title: Greece and Rome
subject: CLAS
description: Introduction to ancient Greek and Roman civilization, focusing on key themes, problems, and methods of the discipline of classical studies.

title: Greek Mythology
subject: CLAS
description: A survey of the myths and legends of Ancient Greece.

title: Introductory Latin 1
subject: CLAS
description: A course designed for beginners with little or no background in Latin. Introduction to basic grammar, vocabulary, morphology. Reading of simple sentences and connected passages.

title: Introductory Latin 2
subject: CLAS
description: Continued introduction to Latin grammar, vocabulary, and morphology. Reading of more complex sentences and longer connected passages.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 210D1/D2 prior to September 2016.

title: Intensive Introductory Latin
subject: CLAS
description: A course designed for beginners with little or no background in Latin. Intensive introduction to grammar, vocabulary, morphology; the reading of sentences and connected passages. Equivalent to CLAS 210 and 212.

title: Introductory Ancient Greek 1
subject: CLAS
description: A course designed for beginners with little or no background in ancient Greek. Introduction to basic grammar, vocabulary, morphology. Reading of simple sentences and connected passages.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 220 D1/D2 prior to September 2016.

title: Introductory Ancient Greek 2
subject: CLAS
description: Continued introduction to ancient Greek grammar, vocabulary, and morphology. Reading of more complex sentences and longer connected passages.
restrictions: Not open to student who have taken CLAS 220D1/D2.

title: Intensive Introductory Ancient Greek
subject: CLAS
description: A course designed for beginners with little or no background in ancient Greek. Intensive introduction to grammar, vocabulary, morphology; the reading of sentences and connected passages. Equivalent to CLAS 220 and 222.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 220 or CLAS 222.

title: Introductory Modern Greek
subject: CLAS
description: A course for beginners.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 236, CLAS 237 or CLAS 238.

title: Introductory Modern Greek
subject: CLAS
description: See CLAS 230D1 for course description.

title: Introduction to Classical Archaeology
subject: CLAS
description: Introduction to the archaeology of the ancient Greek and Roman Mediterranean through a survey of major sites, artifacts and monuments. Emphasis on archaeological theory and methodology.

title: Ancient Greek Literature and Society
subject: CLAS
description: Survey of ancient Greek literature in translation, covering the key genres and texts in their social and historical contexts. The material to be discussed includes Archaic epic, lyric, and elegy; Classical tragedy, comedy, and historiography; Hellenistic poetry, and literature of the Roman Imperial period.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 200.

title: Roman Literature and Society
subject: CLAS
description: An exploration of Roman texts written during the Republican and Imperial periods (200 BCE-400 CE) and the study of social contexts in which they were written.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 208.

title: Ancient Greek Religion
subject: CLAS
description: Focus on the history of Greek religion in the Classical Period. Particular attention will be paid to the Greek concept of divinity, local pantheons, civic festival calendars, the topography of myth and ritual, ideas concerning the afterlife, mystery cults, oracles and games and the literary representations of religion.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): CLAS 203 or HIST 205 or permission of instructor.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 380.

title: Ancient Greek Democracy
subject: CLAS
description: Examines the conceptual history of popular government in the context of Greek political culture, from the 6th century BCE to the Roman conquest of Greece.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): HIST 205 or HIST 231 or permission of instructor.

title: Roman Religion
subject: CLAS
description: Approaches to and problems of Roman religion. The formation of religious topography, problems of religion and empire, the religious interaction between Rome and other Mediterranean peoples, the complex discourse between religion and philosophy, the reformulation of Roman religion during the imperial period, and the rise of Christianity within a pagan Roman world.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 381.

title: Classics in Modern Media
subject: CLAS
description: Receptions of the classical paradigm of Ancient Greece and Rome in modern media, the classical tradition, and current scholarship.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 206.

title: Gender in the Ancient World
subject: CLAS
description: An exploration of gender roles in the Ancient Mediterranean world.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 370.

title: Intermediate Latin 1
subject: CLAS
description: Review of Latin grammar, morphology, syntax, and vocabulary while introducing students to techniques and strategies for reading Latin poetry and prose.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 210 or CLAS 212 or permission of instructor.

title: Intermediate Latin 2
subject: CLAS
description: Continued mastery of the language, with emphasis on translation of Latin texts.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 310 or permission of the instructor.

title: Intermediate Latin 2: Selections
subject: CLAS
description: A study of selected works in Latin.  Topic varies by year.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 310 or permission of the instructor

title: Intermediate Ancient Greek 1
subject: CLAS
description: Review of grammar, vocabulary, and syntax of Ancient Greek through translation of selected ancient texts.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 220 or permission of instructor

title: Intermediate Ancient Greek 2
subject: CLAS
description: Continued mastery of the language, with emphasis on translation of ancient Greek texts.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 320 or permission of the instructor

title: Intermediate Ancient Greek 2: Selections
subject: CLAS
description: Translation of ancient Greek texts selected from a given topic, theme, genre, or author. Texts and authors change from year to year.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s) : CLAS 320 or permission of instructor.

title: Intermediate Modern Greek 1
subject: CLAS
description: Oral and written competence in the language at the intermediate level through the study of grammar and vocabulary. Excerpts from literature, film and music introducing the civilization of modern Greece.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 230 or similar course or permission of the instructor

title: Intermediate Modern Greek 2
subject: CLAS
description: A thorough review of the language at the intermediate level through the study of grammar, vocabulary and derivatives. Excerpts in prose, poetry and newspapers as well as audiovisual material introducing the civilization of modern Greece. a continuation of CLAS 331.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): CLAS 331 or similar course or permission of instructor.

title: Modern Greek Culture and Society
subject: CLAS
description: Offers a panorama of Greek culture and society through the study of a corpus of documents in Greek pertaining to the year's thematic topic.

title: Modern Greek Literature
subject: CLAS
description: Offers a panorama of Modern Greek literature in translation. It examines a corpus of texts selected according to each year's thematic topic of study.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 220 or CLAS 335 or HIST 349 or permission of instructor

title: Life in the Ancient Greek and Roman City
subject: CLAS
description: The impact of cities and urban living in the development of Greek and Roman society. The work of modern urban theorists frames investigation of the urban form and experience, with an emphasis on archaeology.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: CLAS 201, CLAS 240, HIST 205, or permission of the instructor.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 348 when topic was "Life in the Ancient Greek and Roman City".

title: People and Environment in the Ancient World
subject: CLAS
description: The environmental history of the ancient Mediterranean through archaeological and art historical remains. The humanistic and material approaches to what the ancients built, modified, destroyed, and renewed as they engaged with and manipulated the “natural” world and resources around them. The details of what the Mediterranean environment was, and how the Greeks and Romans viewed their environmental contexts, while also shaping them to their needs and wants. Investigation of the Mediterranean’s environmental diversity and consideration of how the ancient context might be informative for our contemporary challenges with climate change.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: CLAS 201, CLAS 240, HIST 205, or permission of the instructor.

title: Topics: Classical Archaeology
subject: CLAS
description: Study of a theme, subject, or question, concentrating on selected physical sites, monuments, artifacts, or other case studies in classical archaeology.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): HIST 205 or CLAS 240 or permission of instructor

title: Archaeology Fieldwork: Italy
subject: CLAS
description: Field course offering an introduction to archaeological field methods and laboratory work, and discussion of theoretical interpretation of archaeological data in the context of an Italian archaeological site potentially across multiple time periods (prehistoric, pre-Roman, Roman, late antique and medieval). Taught in Italy.

title: Special Topics in Classics
subject: CLAS
description: A study of a topic in ancient Greek or Roman literature and culture. Ancient texts taught in translation; students require no knowledge of ancient Greek or Latin. Topics varies by year.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 347.

title: Ancient Drama and Theatre
subject: CLAS
description: A synchronic study of ancient Drama from Greece to Rome with a focus on historical and performance context in addition to literary interpretation.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 300.

title: Ancient Comedy
subject: CLAS
description: A study of ancient Greek and Roman comedy, including authors such as Aristophanes, Menander, Plautus, and Terence. Issues connected to performance, textual interpretation and the social role of comedy will be explored.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 307.

title: Hellenistic Literature and Society
subject: CLAS
description: The cultural legacy of Hellenistic Alexandria, with focus on scientific, mathematical, literary, philological, philosophical, and religious developments and innovations.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): HIST 205 or HIST 231 or permission of the instructor.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 305.

title: The Greek and Roman Novel
subject: CLAS
description: A study of the ancient novel, including Petronius, The Satyricon, Apuleius, The Golden Ass and Longus, Daphnis and Chloe. Issues connected to the novel's development and generic formations, its social and historical contexts, and influence will be discussed.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 309.

title: Classical Tradition
subject: CLAS
description: Examines the evolution of Classical Antiquity's social and cultural status from the 17th c. to the present day. Particular consideration is given to the processes of the ongoing professionalization of history and archeology as academic disciplines, the emergence of new political usages of the past, the transformation of cultural practices from the Grand Tour to the modern museum and tourism.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 202 or related courses or permission of instructor

title: The Epic Tradition
subject: CLAS
description: The course covers major epics of the Mediterranean world such as the Epic of Gilgamesh, Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, Apollonius' Argonautica, Vergil's Aeneid, Ovid's Metamorphoses, Lucan's Bellum Civile, and Statius' Thebaid. Issues connected to social and cultural context, performance, literary theory, and interpretation will be discussed.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 371.

title: Greek and Roman Historiography
subject: CLAS
description: Seminar on the works of the Greek and Roman historians (in translation) who founded a new literary genre for the exploration of past and present events; interpretation of their approaches towards history and theories for their study.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): 3 credits in Classics at the 300 level or up or permission of instructor.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 490.

title: Ancient Lyric and Elegy
subject: CLAS
description: This course examines the Lyric and Elegiac genres from Greece (700 BCE) to Imperial Rome (100 CE). Authors such as Archilochus, Sappho, Alcaeus, Callimachus, Catullus, Propertius and Ovid will be situated in their social and historical contexts as the class addresses issues of poetics, politics, sexuality, and culture.

title: Greek and Roman Oratory
subject: CLAS
description: Greek and Roman Oratory situates the works of authors such as Plato, Demosthenes, Aeschines, Cicero and Tacitus in their social and historical contexts, in addition to examining ancient oratorical theory, education, political science, and culture.

title: Ancient Didactic Poetry
subject: CLAS
description: Ancient Didactic Poetry examines the works of authors such as Hesiod, Empedocles, Aratus, Lucretius, Vergil, Ovid and Manilius. The works are set in their original historical and social contexts while issues related to intellectual history, ancient cosmology, poetry and culture are considered.

title: Advanced Latin: Authors
subject: CLAS
description: Translation and discussion of selections from ancient Latin literature written by a single author or several authors closely linked by genre or historical period. Emphasis on developing reading proficiency. Texts change from year to year. Course may be taken more than once.

title: Advanced Latin: Themes
subject: CLAS
description: Examination of a theme or problem in Roman literature, culture or history through the translation and discussion of ancient Latin texts. Emphasis on close reading and analysis of ancient Latin. Texts change from year to year. Course may be taken more than once.

title: Advanced Ancient Greek: Authors
subject: CLAS
description: Translation and discussion of selections from ancient Greek literature written by a single author or several authors closely linked by genre or historical period. Emphasis on developing reading proficiency. Texts change from year to year. Course may be taken more than once.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): CLAS 322 or permission of instructor

title: Advanced Ancient Greek: Themes
subject: CLAS
description: Examination of a theme or problem in ancient Greek literature, culture or history through the translation and discussion of ancient Greek texts. Emphasis on close reading and analysis of ancient Greek. Texts change from year to year. Course may be taken more than once.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 322 or permission of instructor

title: Medieval Greek
subject: CLAS
description: Readings by Greek authors writing during the Late Imperial through Byzantine periods
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): CLAS 312 or permission of instructor

title: Advanced Topics
subject: CLAS
description: An in-depth look at various topics in classical studies.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): Any ancient history course or 300-level Classics course or permission of instructor.

title:
Greco-Roman Religious
 Literature
subject: CLAS
description: Examination of works of Greek and Roman literature that either deal extensively with theology and religion as themes or were implicated directly in religious practice. Authors or texts such as Hesiod, the Homeric Hymns, Plato, the Derveni Papyrus, Varro, Cicero, Philo and Augustine will be considered.

title: Independent Research
subject: CLAS
description: Under the direction of an instructor, an independent research course that makes use of ancient texts in their original language.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): Written permission of instructor. Student must have extensive background in the proposed area of study.

title: Internship: Classics
subject: CLAS
description: Internship with an approved host institution or organization.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite(s): Permission of the departmental Internship Adviser.
restrictions: Open to U2 and U3 students with a minimum CGPA of 2.7, and permission of the departmental Internship Advisor

title: Classics Seminar
subject: CLAS
description: Seminar on a topic in ancient Greek or Roman literature and society. Topic varies by year.
restrictions: Open to U2 or U3 Honours students and MA students or by permission of instructor

title: Methods in Latin Literature in Translation
subject: CLAS
description: Survey of Latin Literature in translation, confronting questions of genre and situating texts in their social and historical contexts, including epic, lyric, didactic, bucolic, and elegiac poetry; comedy and tragedy, historiography, and rhetoric.

title: Methods in Ancient Greek Literature in Translation 1
subject: CLAS
description: Survey of Ancient Greek Literature in translation, confronting questions of genre and situating texts in their social and historical contexts, including epic, lyric and bucolic poetry; Classical tragedy, comedy, historiography, and rhetoric.

title: Research in Latin Literature in Translation
subject: CLAS
description: Readings, discussion, and research in Classical Latin literature on a specific topic or theme through translated texts.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: CLAS 605 or permission of the instructor

title: Research in Ancient Greek Literature in Translation
subject: CLAS
description: Readings, discussion, and research in Ancient Greek literature on a specific topic or theme through translated texts.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: CLAS 606 or permission of the instructor

title: Intensive Latin Review
subject: CLAS
description: Intensive review of advanced Latin grammar, morphology, syntax and vocabulary, and strategies and techniques for advanced translation prose and poetry.

title: Readings in Latin Literature
subject: CLAS
description: Translation and analysis of selected texts in Latin. Authors or texts change from year to year. This course may be taken more than once.

title: Topics in Latin Literature
subject: CLAS
description: Examination of a selected topic in Latin literature through the translation and analysis of relevant Latin texts. Topics vary by year. Course may be taken more than once.

title: Intensive Ancient Greek Review
subject: CLAS
description: Intensive review of advanced grammar, morphology, syntax and vocabulary of ancient Greek, and strategie and techniques for advanced translation of prose and poetry.

title: Readings in Ancient Greek Literature
subject: CLAS
description: Translation and analysis of selected texts in ancient Greek. Authors or texts change from year to year. This course may be taken more than once.

title: Topics in Ancient Greek Literature
subject: CLAS
description: Examination of a selected topic in ancient Greek literature through the translation and analysis of relevant ancient Greek texts. Topics vary by year. Course may be taken more than once.

title: Methods in Ancient Mediterranean Religion 1
subject: CLAS
description: Topics in ancient Greek and/or Roman religion. Introduction to the historiography of the field, its central questions, theoretical approaches, and methods.

title: Methods in Ancient Mediterranean Religion 2
subject: CLAS
description: Studies in ancient Mediterranean religions. Thematic focus includes ritual and practice, ritual and practice, the concept of the divine and pantheons, the afterlife, the intersection of religion and philosophy, the role of religion in empire, the emergence of Christianity, and its development. Focus on ancient Greek and/or Roman contexts.

title: Research in Ancient Mediterranean Religions
subject: CLAS
description: Readings, discussion, and research on a topic in ancient Greek or Roman religion
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: CLAS 631, CLAS 632, or permission of the instructor

title: Methods in Classical Archaeology 1
subject: CLAS
description: Investigation of the historiography, theoretical approaches, and methods employed in the field of classical archaeology. Focus on the Greek and/or Roman Mediterranean, broadly construed.

title: Methods in Classical Archaeology 2
subject: CLAS
description: Case studies in classical archaeology from the Greek and Roman Mediterranean. Focus on specific sites, objects, and artworks to elaborate broader theoretical and methodological issues in the field.

title: Research in Classical Archaeology
subject: CLAS
description: Readings, discussion, and research on a topic in classical archaeology.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: CLAS 646, CLAS 647, or permission of the instructor

title: Archeological Fieldwork in Italy
subject: CLAS
description: Archaeological fieldwork in Italy; emphasis on archaeological field methods, laboratory work, and theoretical interpretation of archaeological data in an Italian archaeological context. Taught at an archaeological site in Italy.

title: Seminar
subject: CLAS
description: Topics in ancient Greek or Roman literature, culture, and society. Emphasis on the reading and interpretaton of texts in ancient Greek and Latin.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CLAS 691.

title: Methods in Classical Reception 1
subject: CLAS
description: Investigation of the historiography of classical reception as a field, and the theories and methods employed in its study.

title: Methods in Classical Reception 2
subject: CLAS
description: A study of classical reception through case studies that underscore the diversity of media and message through time, and the significance of these patterns of engagement.

title: Research in Classical Reception
subject: CLAS
description: Readings, discussion, and research on a topic in classical reception.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CLAS 653, CLAS 654, or permission of the instructor

title: Modern Greek 1
subject: CLAS
description: Intensive reading of Modern Greek poetry in the original language.

title: Modern Greek 2
subject: CLAS
description: Intensive reading of Modern Greek prose in the original language.

title: M.A.Research Project 1
subject: CLAS
description: Start of the production of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member.

title: M.A.Research Project 2
subject: CLAS
description:
Continued work on production of a research project under the supervision of a faculty
member.

title: M.A.Research Project 3
subject: CLAS
description: Completion of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member.

title: Methods Seminar
subject: CLAS
description: Selected topics in the diverse research methods deployed in classical studies, including (but not limited to) different approaches to interpreting ancient evidence, the acquisition of research skills, grant writing, and publication strategies.

title: M.A. Thesis Proposal
subject: CLAS
description: Preparatory work for the writing of an M.A. thesis under the supervision of the thesis advisor(s), leading to a thesis proposal.

title: M.A. Thesis Research 1
subject: CLAS
description: Continued work for the writing of an M.A. thesis under the supervision of the thesis advisor(s), including production of an annotated bibliography.

title: M.A. Thesis Research 2
subject: CLAS
description: Continued work under the supervision of the thesis advisor(s).

title: M.A. Thesis Submission
subject: CLAS
description: Continued work under the supervision of the thesis advisor(s), leading to completion and submission.

title: Tutorial
subject: CLAS
description: Individualized guided research on an approved topic.

title: Approaches to Multilingualism Management
subject: CMDC
description:
Critical examination of the concept of multilingualism, its management and its social and economic consequences for the public and private sectors. Different models of institutional and corporate multilingualism management, as well as their effects on the language and communication industries will be analyzed. Implications of language technology developments on multilingualism
management.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Translation Literacy in the Digital Age
subject: CMDC
description:
In-depth examination of the specificities of digital communication in translation. Review of research techniques and tools, as well as translation methods, strategies and procedures best suited to a variety of selected translation challenges concerning digital content. Translation exercises involving different text typologies
and genres, ranging from the creative to the technical, each requiring varying degrees of adaptation. Meta-reflection exercises. Ethics and professional best
practices.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Research Methods in Multilingual Digital Communication
subject: CMDC
description: Introduction to applied research in multilingual digital communication. Overview of research design types. Qualitative methods in multilingual research, with an emphasis on interviews, focus groups and usability tests, as well as quantitative methods, with an emphasis on survey research, summative benchmark studies and web analytics. Examination of the fundamental aspects of data collection and data analysis in multilingual research. Overview of report writing and research ethics.
restrictions: Only open to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Language Technologies
subject: CMDC
description: Overview of language technologies for multilingual communication, including computer-assisted translation tools (translation memories, terminology databases, translation and editing environments), project management systems, machine and speech translation systems, and quality evaluation methodologies, from single-purpose solutions to augmented translation interactions. Introduction to industry standards and the role of artificial intelligence in the language industry. Analysis of the principles of creating and managing written and spoken content for multilingual digital communication. Exploration of state-of-the-art language and speech technologies. Introduction to translation management systems and the benefits and challenges of integrating language technology tools into industry workflows.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: CMDC 614 or offering unit approval.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Project Management for Global Content
subject: CMDC
description: Examination of important theoretical concepts and best practices in project management, with a focus on global content and localization. Analysis of localization approaches based on different asset types. Study of all phases of the translation and localization project management lifecycle. Review of project management tools for global content, including automation and artificial intelligence (AI)-powered tools. Stakeholder management, risk management and business intelligence strategies. Application of quality assurance frameworks and tools.
corequisitesText: Corequisites: CMDC 618 or offering unit approval.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Current Trends in Multilingual Digital Communication
subject: CMDC
description: Theoretical and practical exploration of the principles, techniques, challenges and trends of digital and online communication in a global context, with a focus on multilingual contexts. Examination of the role of multilingual digital communication as it relates to or is influenced by online and technological trends. Overview of digital communication platforms for different locales, and outline of the content created for each. Analysis of the role and use of machine translation and other artificial intelligence (AI)- driven applications in multilingual digital communication.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Multilingual Communication
subject: CMDC
description:
Introduction to artificial intelligence (AI), with the goal of understanding the technology, its applications and its impact on professional practices and organizational workflows. How algorithm correctness is attained and how language technology experts can evaluate algorithm bias and contribute to adjusting and optimizing AI applications. Overview of current AI applications in multilingual
communication and organizational processes. Analysis of the applicability of current developments, as well as their impact on the multilingual digital communication industries, society and the human-machine experience.
restrictions: only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Social Media & Community Management in Multilingual Contexts
subject: CMDC
description: Creating and adapting social media content to different locales and engaging and managing online communities in a multilingual context. Focus on developing online identity and presence, and promoting products or services or disseminating information by creating, curating and managing written and visual content on various social media platforms to promote user engagement. Overview of how to adapt content for different digital platforms and locales. The role of a community manager in building, growing and managing multilingual online communities is analyzed.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Technical Writing
subject: CMDC
description:
Best practices and principles in technical writing, including document design. Application to technical writing/communication genres, including product descriptions and specifications, end-user instructions, how-to and troubleshooting guides, user acceptance tests, standard operating procedures, technical reports
and white papers.
restrictions: only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Advanced Language Technology: Evaluation and Implementation
subject: CMDC
description: In-depth examination of computer-assisted translation tools and translation management systems beyond core functionalities, delving into the advanced features that distinguish these systems. Empirical comparative research on language technologies and evaluation methods explored via practical exercises on the best tool, asset and system configuration selection, including IT infrastructure factors. Introduction to software implementation methodologies adapted to language technologies. The key concepts of business analysis and overview of various language technology implementation plans, main risks and mitigation measures, including change management.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Global Digital Communication and Localization Strategies
subject: CMDC
description:
Study and application of the analytical frameworks for strategic communication in a global context to outline a global communications plan that includes a localization strategy. Analysis of key concepts including globalization, internationalization,
localization, translation and transcreation. Analysis of culture-specific content localization for different locales, as well as key considerations regarding technologies and channels, content and engagement, access, and usability of a product or service across cultures.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Translation and Large Language Models
subject: CMDC
description:
Review of machine translation research, along with its history, status, strengths, limitations, user cases and impact on the multilingual digital communication
industries and society at large. Examination of selected natural language processing applications (e.g., neural machine translation, generative artificial intelligence), including engine customization options (e.g., glossaries, machine learning, rule adaptation). Review of the literature on the nature, techniques and best practices associated with machine translation, and application of techniques using large language models on a variety of document types. The use of evaluation metrics to assess the benefits of different translation technologies and
processes in different scenarios.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program

title: Multilingual Content Management in Enterprise Solutions
subject: CMDC
description:
Overview of multilingual content structuring approaches in enterprise solutions and their impact on localization and translation processes. Review of content storage and extraction for translation in a selection of enterprise systems such as content
management systems, web content management systems, product information management systems, and e-learning and e-commerce platforms. Examination of benefits of integrating enterprise solutions and translation management systems to
automate content extraction and integration, and review of key factors to assess feasibility.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

title: Transcreation Lab
subject: CMDC
description: A detailed examination of the specificities of the transcreation process, including Search Engine Optimization (SEO) keyword research, the transcreation client brief and the quoting process for transcreation projects. Execution of a full-fledged transcreation project for a product or brand.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program

title: Data Structure for Language Professionals
subject: CMDC
description:
Localization and internationalization core concepts, processes and best practices as a background to the implications of common data-related pitfalls (e.g., in encoding, multi-byte characters, text directionality, text extraction and file format conversion). File pre- and post-processing, specifications and validation tools, with an emphasis on tagged files (e.g., XML, HTML), industry standards (e.g., XLIFF, TMX, TBX) and advanced desktop publishing formats, as well as file manipulation strategies (e.g., regular expressions, file converters, macros, scripts,
basic database queries).
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

subject: CMDC
description: Supervised non-research project in the student’s stream of choice. Supervised by an academic staff member and/or external partner.
restrictions: Open only to students enrolled in the M.Sc.(Applied) in Multilingual Digital Communication; Non-Thesis program.

subject: CMDC
description: Preparation of applied research proposal and start of research under supervision of an academic staff member. Collaboration with an industry partner is optional.

subject: CMDC

title: Information System Security
subject: CMIS
description: Fundamental concepts relating to the design of secure information systems. Identification and assessment of security risks at the application, network, and physical levels. Use of cryptography and other techniques to provide necessary level of security.

title: Digital Analytics and Targeting
subject: CMIS
description: Covers fundamental techniques in measuring and analysing the digital marketing experience success and effectiveness as well as using audience data to improve advertising and content using targeting and experiments. How to measure, analyze, and act upon the evolving internet technologies and trends.

title: Digital Customer Experience
subject: CMIS
description:
Covers the fundamental techniques for understanding, analyzing and optimizing
customer experience on digital platforms. Explores best practices in designing and optimizing conversion actions in an online business. Management of customer data and confidentiality.

title: Digital Marketing Automation, Planning and Technology
subject: CMIS
description: Covers the fundamental concepts needed to develop a digital marketing plan. Enables students to gain an understanding of market behaviour, translation of corporate goals into digital marketing objectives, basic overview of various strategic approaches to align to objectives, as well as implementation and control.

title: Cloud Computing Architecture
subject: CMIS
description:
Covers different cloud infrastructures and architectures in the context of deployed cloud computing systems that are appropriate for different businesses. Enables
students to use key business metrics to make decisions on the suitability of applications for cloud deployment.

title: Digital Media and Search Engine Optimization
subject: CMIS
description: Covers the fundamentals of promoting a brand through digital mediums and how to take advantage of earned digital media. Provides an understanding of how paid search, search engine optimization, various forms of digital media planning and placement, social media promotion work and, how to monitor and optimize performance.

title: Information Systems for Managers
subject: CMIS
description:
Introduction to the importance of information systems (IS) and the digital transformation of companies from a managerial perspective. Overview of the strategic importance of information technology (IT) and IS, including implementing IS and IT projects for creating and capturing value and making companies more
competitive. Consideration of managerial, informational, and technological issues arising from the use of IS, IT, and their respective processes. Application of a strategic framework for managing companies, especially digitized companies, more effectively.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CMIS 541.

title: Indigenous Peoples and the State
subject: CMPL
description: Current legal topics relating to Indigenous peoples, including the concept of Indigenous title, and constitutional aspects of contemporary land claims. Aspects of Canadian law relating to Indigenous peoples, their constitutional status, and hunting and fishing rights.

title: Jurisprudence
subject: CMPL
description: The main schools of jurisprudence and the most significant writings, particularly contemporary writings, in legal philosophy.

title: Canon Law
subject: CMPL
description: History, sources and methods of interpretation of canon law, its influence on secular legal traditions, its codification, and its contemporary relevance.

title: Feminist Legal Theory
subject: CMPL
description: Feminist theory and its relevance and application to law, including feminist methodologies in law, the public versus private dichotomy, and changing conceptions of equality.

title: Legal Theory
subject: CMPL
description: The philosophical basis of private law, from a comparative and historical perspective.

title: Social Diversity and Law
subject: CMPL
description: The interaction of law and cultural diversity. Through the use of a number of case studies, we will examine: 1. The empirical effect of cultural diversity on legal systems. 2. Institutional structures to accommodate diversity. 3. Theoretical perspectives.

title: Theories of Justice
subject: CMPL
description: The concept of political justice and its relationship to particular legal and economic institutions, including the moral foundations of theories of justice, the nature of legitimate political authority, and the nature of distributive justice.

title: Talmudic Law
subject: CMPL
description: Historical sources of Talmudic law, methods of interpretation, selected topics, and relation to various secular legal traditions.

title: International Carriage of Goods by Sea
subject: CMPL
description: A comparative study of private international maritime law.

title: International Development Law
subject: CMPL
description: The law and economics of development, including the role of agencies of the United Nations in development, the role of UNCTAD in formulating uniform rules of international trade, and the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund and their role in financing development.

title: Public Policy, Politics and Law
subject: CMPL
description: How law and politics shape public policy-making and implementation. The focus will be on how policy preferences and political decisions get ‘translated’ into legal instruments. The interaction of politics and law in the making of various public policies may be explored within a single jurisdiction or a particular policy may be examined across multiple jurisdictions.

title: Comparative Modern Legal History
subject: CMPL
description: Advanced seminar in contemporary methods of legal history, comparative theories of history, representative North Atlantic historiographical traditions, and especially select issues in modern legal history. Issues include professionalization, institutionalizing customary norms state formation, application of state law, and official normativity in popular culture.

title: Medical Liability
subject: CMPL
description: Trans-systemic and critical examination of medical liability issues, including doctor-hospital-patient relationship; medical duty of care; medical fault and causation; wrongful life, birth and conception; informed consent and refusal; lack of resources; defective products; nosocomial infections; contaminated blood transfusions; interaction between law and science; future of medical liability.
restrictions: Not open to students in first year of Law.

title: Entertainment Law
subject: CMPL
description: This course is designed to introduce students to the rules governing the Canadian entertainment industry in an international context with particular emphasis on the television, film production and distribution industries. There will also be limited coverage of the law relating to the music industry. The course will consider inter alia the contractual, tax, financial and insurance aspects of the law applicable to the entertainment industry.

title: Resolution of International Disputes
subject: CMPL
description: Conflict of jurisdictions and recognition of foreign judgments, as well as arbitration between parties to international contracts, with particular reference to  international conventions.

title: European Union Law 1
subject: CMPL
description: The Treaty of Rome establishing the European Community and current efforts to create a homogenous structure for commerce and competition in Europe.

title: European Union Law 2
subject: CMPL
description: The provisions of the Treaty of Rome dealing with the regulation of domestic and international commerce by the Community authorities, with particular emphasis on articles 85 and 86.

title: International Taxation
subject: CMPL
description: Canadian tax treatment of subjects, including the export of goods and services, carrying on business in other countries, international employee transfers, international re-organizations, and international joint ventures and partnerships.

title: Law and Practice of International Trade
subject: CMPL
description: The fundamental aspects of international law governing international trade, and governmental regulation of international trade in Canada and Canada's major trading partners.

title: International Environmental Law and Politics
subject: CMPL
description: Examination of institutions and processes for global environmental protection. Consideration of means for advancing international cooperation for environmental protection, focusing on international law. Analysis of obstacles to applying international law to environmental problems. Examination of a range of governance structures for environmental protection and the way in which they operate.

title: Canadian Legal History
subject: CMPL
description: The history of Canadian law with emphasis on social history of law and legal history of Canadian society.

title: International Maritime Conventions
subject: CMPL
description: International maritime conventions in respect of collisions, jurisdiction, limitation of liability, and their domestic interpretation, maritime liens and mortgages, marine insurance, and salvage.

title: International Humanitarian Law
subject: CMPL
description: Rules governing international and internal armed conflicts; historical and philosophical foundations; constraints on means to wage war; treatment of protected individuals, including prisoners of war, civilians and peacekeepers; enforcement, including belligerent reprisals and criminal prosecution; links with norms protecting human rights, the environment and cultural property; impact of cultural diversity.
restrictions: Not open to first year students.

title: Extrajudicial Dispute Resolution
subject: CMPL
description: An examination for the non-adjudicative means of dispute resolution, including mediation and consensual arbitration.
restrictions: Not open to students in the first year of Law.

title: International Law of Human Rights
subject: CMPL
description: International protection of human rights, particularly by the United Nations, its specialized agencies, and the Council of Europe.

title: Civil Liberties
subject: CMPL
description: The protection of civil liberties in Canada with particular reference to public and private law remedies and emphasis on discrimination, race relations, language rights outside the Charter, and police powers.

title: Government Control of Business
subject: CMPL
description: Selected topics in government control and regulation of business with emphasis on competition law and policy.

title: Discrimination and the Law
subject: CMPL
description: Equality rights and legal protections against discrimination under the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, the Quebec Charter of Human Rights and Freedoms, and human rights legislation.

title: Science Technology and Law
subject: CMPL
description: Introduction to the philosophy of science and the history of technology, reciprocal influences of science and law and their parallel development, concepts common to law and science, and legal and ethical problems common to technological change.

title: Communications Law
subject: CMPL
description: Regulation of common communication carriers and mass media in Canada, including legal developments initiated by foreign market competition, and the regulatory authority of the C.R.T.C.

title: Environment and the Law
subject: CMPL
description: Environmental law, with emphasis on ecological, economic, political, and international dimensions.

title: Legal Traditions
subject: CMPL
description: Examination of the concept of a legal tradition, including elements of particular legal traditions, their philosophical foundations, their implementation through institutions, and their influence on one another.
restrictions: Restricted to students in the Institute of Comparative Law. Other students by permission only.

title: Human Rights and Cultural Diversity
subject: CMPL
description: Current topics in human rights and cultural diversity.

title: International Business Law
subject: CMPL
description: Current topics in international business law.

subject: CMPL
description: Legal research methodology, including electronic legal research and the formulation of research plans.

title: Law and Health Care
subject: CMPL
description: The study of legal and ethical issues raised in medicine and healthcare with a particular focus upon the relationship between patient and healthcare professionals.

title: Comprehensive Examination-Comparative Law
subject: CMPL
description: An examination comprised of written and oral components that must be passed by all doctoral candidates in order to continue in the doctoral program.
restrictions: D.C.L. graduate students in Comparative Law.

title: Global Marketing Management
subject: CMR2
description: Marketing management considerations of a company seeking to extend beyond the confines of its domestic market. A review of product, pricing, channels of distribution and communications policies to develop an optimum strategy (between adapting completely to each local environment and standardizing across them) for arriving at an integrated and profitable operation. Particular attention to international marketing and exporting in the Canadian context.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: (CMR2 542 or CMR2 642) and CMR2 548 or CMR2 648 or CMS2 521.

title: Digital Marketing Communications
subject: CMR2
description: Applies a strategic approach to developing and measuring a digital marketing communication strategy for various platforms and channels aligned to the traditional marketing communications mix. Covers how to leverage best practices to optimise online community building, conversion, and customer experience through digital channels in an integrated marketing communication strategy.

title:
Marketing Principles and
 Applications
subject: CMR2
description:
Examination of the different aspects of marketing operations: the marketing concept, analysis and research of market opportunities, and the planning, implementation, and control of the marketing program (product, promotion,
distribution, and pricing). Focus is on the general market environment and Canadian marketing institutions.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CMR2 542.

title:
Marketing of
 Services
subject: CMR2
description:
Review of the concepts, frameworks, and current trends in the marketing of services, including new creative products. Analysis of issues pertaining to the delivery of service excellence, effective communication, the highest quality, and
loyalty. Focus is on service marketing in the private and public sectors.

title:
Marketing Research and
 Reporting
subject: CMR2
description: Review of statistics, with emphasis on key concepts required to understand and report marketing information. Overview of qualitative and quantitative data collection techniques and interpretation of secondary on-line research. Focus on Facebook and Google analytics and insights.

title:
Digital Marketing
 Management
subject: CMR2
description: Overview of digital and web-based marketing principles and areas such as social media, search engine optimization, search engine marketing, content marketing, email marketing, and e-commerce. Design of digital strategies to drive business growth.

title:
Integrated Marketing
 Communications
subject: CMR2
description: Design of an integrated marketing plan, including creativity, branding, media selection, customer segmentation, and budgeting. Strategic approach to the integrated marketing mix: digital promotion, advertising, public relations, experiential marketing, and direct marketing.

title: Buyer Behaviour
subject: CMR2
description: Comprehensive overview of the behaviour of the consumer in the marketplace and the research approaches to analyzing and understanding that behaviour. Exploration of human behaviour and action in the marketing context with a focus on the basic processes of consumer decision-making.

title: Marketing Strategy
subject: CMR2
description:
Development of a complete strategic marketing plan including the allocation of resources.
Formulation of a marketing strategy for real-world cases.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken CMR2 570.

title: Fundamentals of Marketing
subject: CMRK
description: Fundamental theories and principles of strategic marketing. Role of the marketing professional in the corporate environment. Applications of marketing practices to new businesses. Development of a marketing plan.

title: Marketing Statistics and Research
subject: CMRK
description: Basic statistics for marketing research. Qualitative and quantitative data collection techniques, traditional and digital. Use of secondary on-line data: determining reliability, interpretation, analysis.

title: Digital Media Marketing
subject: CMRK
description: Electronic marketplaces and their evolving role in Internet business. New channels of marketing, including social media, advertising and communication.  Planning, executing, and managing e-commerce.  Web analytics, customer analysis, search engine optimization, search engine marketing and issues of permission and privacy.

title: Principles of Consumer Behaviour
subject: CMRK
description: Foundational and emerging concepts of consumer behaviour. Perception, learning, attitude formation and change, decision-making, social influences, motivations, values, lifestyle, geo-demographics and the dynamics of reference groups in social media. Ethical and responsible use of digital marketing tools.

title: Integrated Marketing Communications
subject: CMRK
description: Marketing communications mix:  advertising (in both traditional and digital media), publicity, promotion, creative tactics, direct marketing, marketing-oriented public relations, buzz creation, and sponsorships. Communication theory and ethical practice. Use and effects of social media

title: Basics of Service Marketing
subject: CMRK
description: Differences between marketing of products and of services. Marketing mix for service business. Balance of supply and demand. Permissible nature of a service in relation to time. Value and quality of services. Managing service operations. Customer satisfaction.

title: Global Marketing
subject: CMRK
description: Issues faced by businesses when entering and operating in foreign markets: changes in product, pricing, channels, and communications policies. Export marketing in the Canadian context.

title: Marketing Applications
subject: CMRK
description: Integrative, capstone course: cultivating skills and techniques required for effective marketing planning. Application of theories and skills learned in previous courses. Situational analysis and problem-solving skills. Cases and marketing simulation.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisites: CMRK 200, CMRK 225, CMRK 235, CMRK 320, CMRK 321, CMRK 322, CMRK 325, CPRL 221 and (CMRK 230 or CGMG 318)

title: Mathematics for Management
subject: CMS2
description: Basic mathematics needed for business applications, including graphs of functions, series summation, mathematics of finance, annuity, discounted cash flow, internal rate of return, permutations, combinations, maxima and minima of functions with business applications in optimization, introductory statistics and probability

title: Management of Service Operations
subject: CMS2
description: The course takes an operations point of view to look at companies and industries in the services sector. It builds on conceptual frameworks and cases from a wide range of service operations, selected from health care, hospitality, internet services, transportation, retailing, financial services, humanitarian services, government services, and others.

title: Supply Chain Management
subject: CMS2
description: This is an applications-oriented course in supply chain strategy and macro-processes of supply chain management such as supplier relations management, customer relations management, logistics and distribution. Use of operations research models and computer software will be an integral part of this course.

title: Re-Engineering and Integration of Business Systems
subject: CMS2
description: Information systems used in supply chains are presented in the context of enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems with applications in manufacturing, retailing and distribution services sectors. Core business processes and transactions pertaining to supply chain management are identified and discussed in terms of relevant ERP modules.

title: Lean Operations and Performance Management in Health Services
subject: CMS2
description: Role of operations management and how to create public value by delivering services effectively and efficiently, and measure the performance of the organization, including how the lean approach in healthcare can provide “outside of the box” solutions to resolve process issues and improve quality, cost and delivery of healthcare services.

title: Lean Operations and Performance Management in Health Services
subject: CMS2
description: Role of operations management and how to create public value by delivering services effectively and efficiently, and measure the performance of the organization, including how the lean approach in healthcare can provide “outside of the box” solutions to resolve process issues and improve quality, cost and delivery of healthcare services.

title: Lean Operations and Performance Management in Health Services
subject: CMS2
description: Role of operations management and how to create public value by delivering services effectively and efficiently, and measure the performance of the organization, including how the lean approach in healthcare can provide “outside of the box” solutions to resolve process issues and improve quality, cost and delivery of healthcare services.

title: Special Topics in Mathematics
subject: CMS2
description: Intended for students studying at the graduate level in programs requiring specific mathematics skills. Covers intermediate and advanced concepts and selected topics in mathematics.

title: Applied Management Statistics
subject: CMS2
description: Statistical methods used in a variety of business situations, emphasizing application and providing a working knowledge of the most widely-used techniques. Topics include descriptive statistics; probability distributions; sampling procedures and distributions; inferential statistics including estimation; hypothesis testing and Anova; simple linear, multiple regression and correlation; time series and forecasting.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CMS2 500 or the Exemption by Examination Test

title: Business Intelligence and Analytics
subject: CMS2
description:
This course provides a managerial and technical focus on computational and business techniques which can help to identify new business opportunities
and transform an organization’s future by optimizing operational and strategic decision making.

title: Foundations of Mathematics
subject: CMSC
description: First-degree equations and applied word problems, polynomials, factoring, fractions, exponents, roots and radicals, inequalities, quadratic equations and functions, composite and inverse functions, arithmetic and geometric sequences and series.

title: Foundations of Logarithms,Trigonometry & Intro to Calculus
subject: CMSC
description:
Introduction to logarithms and trigonometry. Topics include logs and exponents, using linear equations, limits and differentiation, continuity, derivatives, and introduction to
integral calculus.

title:
Foundations:Statistics,
 Probability&Intro to Linear Algebra
subject: CMSC
description: Statistics and probability, with an introduction to linear algebra, Gaussian elimination for solving linear systems, and an introduction to vectors and matrices in the context of linear systems.

title: Mathematical Tools for Management Professionals
subject: CMSC
description: Exponential and logarithmic functions and equations, mathematics of finance, permutations and combinations, introduction to probability, limits and derivatives with applications, matrices and systems of linear equations.
prerequisitesText: Prerequisite: CMSC 000 Foundations of Mathematics or Diagnostic Test

title: Topics in Foundations of Mathematics
subject: CMSC
description: A selection of introductory topics in the foundations of mathematics.

title: Topics in Applied Mathematics
subject: CMSC
description: A selection of intermediate-level topics in applied mathematics.

title: Survey of Basic Mathematics 1
subject: CMSC
description: Review of analytic geometry, limits, continuity, the derivative, differentiation rules, curve sketching, application to economics, elasticity, problems in optimization, related rates, the differential, log and exponential, continuous compounding, partial differentiation, method of Lagrange multipliers, method of least squares.

title: Managerial Economics and Analysis
subject: CMSC
description:
An overview of the economic theories as well as the internal and external economic factors that influence business so as to apply and understand managerial
decision-making tools. Consideration will be paid to foundational topics such as theories of supply and demand; consumer behaviour; production, cost and
pricing strategies; market structures; and optimization techniques.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken or are taking MGCR 293

title: Business Statistics
subject: CMSC
description: An overview of descriptive statistics, probability, random variables, binomial, Poisson, normal distributions, sampling distribution of the mean, estimation, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, tests of goodness of fit, linear and multiple regression, non-parametric statistics. Business and management case studies will be used.
restrictions: Not open to students who have taken or are taking MGCR 273
